questions.question: What is the key difference between holding an equity share and holding a corporate bond of a company?
options: Shareholders are creditors; bondholders are owners
Bondholders are creditors entitled to contractual interest and principal; shareholders are equity owners sharing in profits and losses
Bondholders have voting rights on the Board of Directors
Corporate bonds never have a maturity date
questions.explanation: A bondholder is a lender/creditor who receives contracted interest and principal repayment before any dividend distribution to shareholders.

questions.question: What does a credit rating of 'AAA' assigned by CRISIL or ICRA signify?
options: Speculative grade with high default risk
Highest degree of safety regarding timely servicing of financial obligations
Backed directly by the Reserve Bank of India
Exempt from all income taxes
questions.explanation: AAA is the highest domestic credit rating, indicating negligible credit default risk based on rating agency analysis.

questions.question: In July 2024, what change did SEBI introduce regarding the face value of privately placed corporate bonds?
options: Increased face value to ₹10 lakh to ban retail investors
Reduced minimum face value from ₹1,00,000 to ₹10,000 to improve retail participation
Abolished corporate bonds altogether
Required all bonds to be physical certificates
questions.explanation: SEBI reduced ticket sizes for privately placed debt to ₹10,000 to make corporate debt accessible to everyday retail investors.

questions.question: What is the primary role of a Debenture Trustee in a corporate bond issue?
options: To trade bonds on behalf of the company for quick profits
To protect bondholders' legal interests, monitor collateral security, and initiate recovery in case of default
To promise 20% annual returns to retail investors
To write analyst opinions on news channels
questions.explanation: Debenture Trustees are SEBI-registered institutions legally tasked with safeguarding debenture holders and enforcing security charges.

questions.question: How is coupon interest from listed corporate bonds taxed for retail individuals?
options: 100% tax-free under all conditions
Added to total income and taxed at the investor's marginal slab rate (with 10% TDS under Section 193 where applicable)
Flat 5% with indexation
Exempt up to ₹5 lakh per year
questions.explanation: Interest from corporate debentures is taxed as income from other sources at the investor's marginal income tax slab rate.
